items.followUp: State one difference between a plant cell wall and a cell membrane.

rubric.why: The primary wall is relatively thin and is formed while the cell grows.
rubric.description: Describes the primary cell wall as thin or formed during growth.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the primary wall is thin or forms during growth.

rubric.why: The secondary wall is deposited inside the primary wall after growth and adds thickness and rigidity.
rubric.description: Describes the position, timing, and greater thickness or rigidity of the secondary cell wall.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the secondary wall forms inside the primary wall after growth and is thicker or more rigid.

modelAnswer: The primary cell wall is thin and flexible and forms during growth.
The secondary cell wall is deposited inside the primary wall after growth and is thicker and more rigid.

items.followUp: What is the role of turgor pressure in a plant cell?

rubric.why: Turgor pressure is the pressure exerted by the contents of a cell on its wall.
rubric.description: Defines turgor pressure as pressure exerted by cell contents against the cell wall.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the pressure and the cell contents or cytoplasm and cell wall involved.

rubric.why: Water entering the cell produces the pressure against the cell wall.
rubric.description: Links turgor pressure to water entering the cell.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that water enters or is taken up by the cell.

modelAnswer: Turgor pressure is the pressure exerted by the cell contents against the cell wall.
It develops when water enters the cell.

items.followUp: Differentiate between asexual and sexual reproduction.

rubric.why: Germline cells give rise to gametes and carry hereditary information to offspring.
rubric.description: Identifies germline cells as cells that form gametes.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that germline cells form gametes.

rubric.why: Somatic cells make up the body and are distinct from germline cells.
rubric.description: Identifies somatic cells as body cells other than germline cells.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing somatic cells as body cells distinct from germline cells.

modelAnswer: Germline cells form gametes and pass genetic information to offspring.
Somatic cells are body cells other than germline cells.

items.followUp: Write the balanced equation for cellular respiration.

rubric.why: The definition identifies the use of light energy to produce glucose from carbon dioxide and water.
rubric.description: Defines photosynthesis and includes its raw materials and use of light energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that green plants use light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water.

rubric.why: The equation shows the balanced amounts of reactants and products.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the balanced equation showing six carbon dioxide and six water molecules forming glucose and six oxygen molecules.

modelAnswer: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water.
6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂ (in the presence of light and chlorophyll).

items.followUp: Why is the electron transport pathway in cellular respiration called a respiratory chain?

rubric.why: The light-reaction electron pathway involves both photosystems.
rubric.description: Identifies the involvement of two photosystems.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both photosystems or stating that two photosystems are involved.

rubric.why: Changes in electron energy during transfer create a profile resembling the letter Z.
rubric.description: Explains that the electron-energy profile or electron flow forms a Z shape.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking the electron flow or energy-level changes to a Z-shaped profile.

modelAnswer: The Z-scheme involves electron transfer through two photosystems, Photosystem II and Photosystem I.
The electron flow and energy level changes during transfer form a Z shape, so the pathway is called the Z-scheme.
